ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is glossy black with iridescent blue reflections and a white-spotted venter. It features a blunt, rounded head and a short, spine-tipped tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Melanophidium wynaudense* is best distinguished by its highly iridescent, glossy black scales and the presence of a distinct yellow or white spot on each ventral scale.
ai.habitat: The Indian Black Earth Snake inhabits moist, evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Black Earth Snake is strictly nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms and other small subterranean prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Melanophidium wynaudense* is viviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Black Earth Snake is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Karnataka at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
